input.text: White Cloud Temple is the Vatican of Chinese Taoism — the headquarters of the Complete Perfection school, and a working monastery since the thirteen hundreds. Its story centers on Qiu Chuji, the Taoist master who crossed deserts and mountains at age seventy-three to counsel Genghis Khan — the khan, impressed, granted him this temple and exemption from taxes. The temple's origins reach back to the Tang dynasty, though fire and rebuilds keep rewriting its fabric. Inside: halls of the Taoist immortals, the grave shrine of Qiu Chuji, and one beloved ritual — hunt the three stone monkeys carved around the courtyard; locals rub them for luck, and finding all three is said to take a lifetime of visits. At Spring Festival, the temple fair here is Beijing's oldest Taoist celebration. Under the pines, incense smoke and quiet chanting — a completely different Beijing than the palaces next door.
